text:
jia: quick follow-up from the offload-placement RFC experiments — we saw a steady increase in small-slab fragmentation after about 12h of mixed workloads. reproducer attached in test cluster.
kevin: ugh, saw that too. is this the 'many 4kb-ish allocations' pattern? :thinking_face:
sana: yeah, mostly tiny kv-cache allocations + some pinned embeddings. fragmentation metric (frag_ratio) goes from ~8% to ~28% over 12h.
jia: exactly. the current soft-reserve per-pool helps throughput but makes compaction less frequent. thinking we need a tenant-aware soft-reserve + compaction hint API.
matt: propose adding two things:
- allocator.soft_reserve(tenant_id, bytes)
- allocator.compact_hint(tenant_id, urgency="background"|"now")

example usage:
```
// rough sketch
allocator.soft_reserve("tenant-42", 128*1024*1024);
if (hotset_shrinking(tenant)) allocator.compact_hint("tenant-42", "background");
if (eviction_pressure > 0.9) allocator.compact_hint("tenant-42", "now");
```

kevin: sounds reasonable. questions: who owns scheduling of compaction work? allocator or admission controller?
sana: my vote: allocator schedules compaction but exposes backpressure signals so admission can slow down. keeping scheduling local avoids cross-service races.
jia: agree. also want to attach a suggested 'frag_threshold' and a 'max_compact_bytes' per-tenant so compaction doesn't thrash.
matt: tradeoffs: more per-tenant state means more memory & bookkeeping. but gives us ability to do proportional compaction across noisy tenants.
kevin: can we piggyback on existing KV of tenant metadata? or does allocator need local fast-path state?
sana: allocator needs fast-path counters (hotset estimate, alloc histogram). storing config in central KV and caching works for policy bits.
offload-bot: snapshot: offload/frag-followup created by jia at 1732468100
jia: also noticed that eviction order when compacting interacts badly with prefix-caching in runtime — compacting a slab that contains many prefixes causes increased misses.
matt: hmm — maybe compaction should prefer areas not covered by prefix cache or we should mark prefix-backed pages as compact-protected for a TTL.
kevin: that gets complex. alternative: compaction produces a small window where runtime can re-warm prefix cache from compacted pages on access (cheap prefetch on first miss).
sana: re-warm strategy seems promising; we can prioritize compaction to avoid high-rt pages and then let lazy re-warm fill cache.
jia: next steps proposal:
1) add soft_reserve & compact_hint into allocator API (minimal surface)
2) allocator maintains per-tenant frag counters + compaction budget
3) admission controller subscribes to compaction/backpressure events
4) runtime adds a re-warm hook that triggers small prefetch on first post-compact miss

kevin: +1 to prototype. who wants to own the RFC for the API shape? I'll take the allocator side docs, jia can draft runtime re-warm hook.
matt: I'll do an experiment: simulate tenants with different tiny allocation mixes and test compaction budgets.
sana: I'll wire the admission controller events and try a canary on staging cluster.
jia: thanks all. I'll open a PR with a minimal API spec and a perf test plan. trying to keep the initial API intentionally small to iterate fast. :thumbsup:
kevin: awesome. ping if you want help with benchmarks or the histograms.
matt: will post initial simulation results in this thread when ready.
offload-bot: deploybot: canary deploy scheduled for staging at 1732469000 (no automatic rollouts)
jia: noted. follow-ups in PR and I'll add a checklist for observability metrics we need (frag_ratio per-tenant, compact_cycles, rewarm_hits).
kevin: sounds good. closing loop: timeline? aim for a small canary in 2 weeks?
